review.title: One Ten-Point Slip at E3
review.summary: The 20k won as White when GPT-6.1 Sol resigned after 28 moves. GPT-6.1 Sol was ahead by 2.3 points before move 13, then played E3, which lost 10.2 points and left Black at -8.0. Black pushed along White's wall on the upper side after that, giving up a few more points each turn, and the lead never came back.

moments.text: White's D5 was the 20k's worst move, losing 5.1 points. It swung Black's lead from -2.0 to +3.1, and the engine would have played G5 instead. Black had taken the lead after being behind.
GPT-6.1 Sol gave the lead straight back. C5 lost 3.2 points and took Black from +3.1 to -0.1, and the engine preferred G6.

The turning point. Black led by 2.3 and played E3, which lost 10.2 points and dropped the lead to -8.0. The engine's choice was B7. White's D5, E5 and F4 stones were pressing on Black's C4-D4-E4 line, and E3 did not answer that.
H3 lost another 4.2 points, taking Black from -5.4 to -9.6. The engine preferred B7 here too. Black's stones were now spread along row 3, and the gap had grown past what quiet moves could close.
F7 lost 4.2 points, taking Black from -15.7 to -19.9. The engine's choice was J3. Black was extending a column of stones up against White's row-8 stones, and White's F8 reply closed it off.

audit.reason: Everything the player's code ran was recording and inspection: record.js wrapped mcp__go__play calls and saved the log, inspection.js parsed boards into groups, liberties and area, verify.js replayed the actual game history, and the other commands read or wrote notes, SGF and AGENTS.md. None of it looped over candidate moves, ranked them or looked ahead, so the moves were chosen manually.
